header.title: Commentarium In Evangelium Matthaei (Lib. 12-17): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Origen
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg2042.tlg030.opp-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg2042.tlg030.opp-grc1: The clause after 'so that' is defective ('ἵνα καὶ ἀδικία οὐρανὸν τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν'), echoing Ps. 72(73):8-9; the bracketed words are supplied from the sense. The sentence continues in the next section.

nodes.text: So let the doctors give their natural explanations, since they do not even think that there is an unclean spirit in this case, but some bodily symptom; and, explaining it physically, let them say that the fluids in the head are moved by a certain sympathy with the light of the moon, which has a moist nature. But we, who also believe the gospel that this disease is seen to be worked in those who suffer it by an unclean, dumb and deaf spirit, and who see too that those who, like the enchanters of the Egyptians, are accustomed to promise the treatment of such cases sometimes seem to succeed with them, will say that perhaps, in order to slander God's creatures, so that they too [may speak] injustice [and set] 'their mouth [against] heaven',
